Fecund

FEE-kund · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Fecund is highly fertile or productive, capable of producing abundant results, offspring, or growth.

Marine biologists were amazed by how fecund the coral reef was, teeming with more new fish hatchlings each season than any other reef in the region.

Worked Example

The old orchard, though neglected for years, proved surprisingly fecund once it was pruned, producing baskets of apples from branches everyone had assumed were dead.

Fecund describes something exceptionally capable of producing abundant results -- crops, offspring, or ideas -- here, the orchard turned out to be far more productive than expected.

How Fecund Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

fertile

fertile: capable of producing abundant crops, growth, or offspring

prolific

prolific: producing a large quantity of something

Antonyms

barren

barren: incapable of producing crops, growth, or offspring

sterile

sterile: unable to produce offspring or results

How Strong Is It? — productive → fecund → teeming

productive vs. fecund

productive vs. fecund: To be productive is simply to get good results or output, a much more everyday word than fecund's specific sense of abundant fertility.

teeming vs. fecund

teeming vs. fecund: Something teeming is so overflowing with life or activity that it seems to burst at the seams, an even more intense image than fecund.

Build the Word

The pieces

root (uncertain family) — fecund-

root (uncertain family) — fecund-: fruitful, productive -- from Latin fecundus, whose deeper origin is debated and never spread into a family of common English words (Latin fecundus)

Put it together

Put it together: Fecund comes from Latin fecundus, meaning 'fruitful' or 'productive.' Unlike many words in this unit, its ultimate root is uncertain and it never grew into a large family of everyday English words -- fecund is mostly a standalone case, related only distantly to the rarer word fecundity.

Use the root in a new word: fertility

Use the root in a new word: fertility: Scientists studied the soil's fertility to understand why some fields produced far larger harvests than others. (Fertility isn't related to fecund by root, but it describes the very same idea of abundant productiveness.)
